Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D., Md.) is doing the unthinkable and challenging Sen. Chuck Schumer (D., N.Y.) and the winner will become next year’s Senate majority leader. This is one of the most powerful jobs in Washington, and perhaps far outside. Control the Senate agenda. Decide who gets confirmed. Stand toe to toe with President Trump. Lead the Democratic Party into the future.

   Republicans have had their share of congressional leadership mutinies (on the House side), but challenges like this aren’t common. Schumer helped Democrats navigate the 2026 midterms and emerge with a gigantic majority next year (picking up either eight or nine seats, depending on what happens in Alaska).

   To oust him now might seem counterintuitive.

   But 2026 is over (well, not technically), but 2028 has begun. Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan has signaled that he would prefer Van Hollen. Sen. John Fetterman (D., Pa.) has hinted he would leave the party if Van Hollen gets the job. Schumer is 75, but this isn’t exactly a past versus the future kind of standoff. Van Hollen is 67 and was first elected to Congress in 2002.

   Democrats are still struggling to reconcile with their position on Israel and how they want to stand up to Trump during his final two years in office. The Democratic Party that won a couple of weeks ago is different and might not be as beholden to the old ways of politicking as the one Schumer has long been a part of.

   This will be a secret ballot, but it would be a huge upset for Van Hollen to knock Schumer from his perch. One thing this could do, though, is create a moment for Democrats to try to extract promises from Schumer that might suit their home-state interests. Will he need to cut deals, or is he about to sail to another big victory?

The agency issued a long-awaited restriction on shipments of chips from Nvidia and other U.S. companies to China, the latest sign of how the Jensen Huang saga is influencing the Trump administration’s policies. Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil will be added to a list of countries subject to export rules.

   Mamdani disbands controversial NYPD unit. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has scrapped the police unit that responds to protests, after he faced increasing pressure to fulfill a promise he had made during the campaign in the wake of anti-ICE protests this fall. The unit, known as the Strategic Response Group , is in charge of making arrests at demonstrations, but protesters and civil liberties groups have long complained about the unit’s tactics.

   Trump’s advisers are at war over China ahead of Xi summit. When Trump boarded Air Force One on Monday for a flight to Asia, he brought with him a team of top advisers who have spent the past week feuding over China policy and blaming one another for the political fallout from the Nvidia scandal. The clashes reflect a fundamental divide over whether the economic deals and friendly relations Trump has pursued with Beijing are worth the national-security vulnerabilities some senior U.S. officials believe they could create for decades.

The agency issued a long-awaited restriction on shipments of chips from Nvidia and other U.S. companies to China, the latest sign of how the Jensen Huang saga is influencing the Trump administration’s policies.
